svyexpo

svyexpo links geocoded household surveys (DHS, MICS, or your own) to raster exposures and fits Bayesian spatial models of exposure–outcome associations, including effects that vary across space.

Existing packages such as SUMMER and surveyPrev focus on small-area prevalence mapping. svyexpo focuses on associations: how much an environmental exposure (PM₂.₅, greenness, temperature) changes an outcome, and where that effect is stronger or weaker.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("niiattey/svyexpo")

# INLA is needed for model fitting and is not on CRAN:
install.packages("INLA",
  repos = c(getOption("repos"), INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"),
  dep = TRUE)

# Needed for spatially varying coefficients (posterior sampling):
install.packages("sn")

Requires R >= 4.1. Modules 1-4 (ingest, boundaries, exposure linkage, adjacency) work without INLA; only model fitting and posterior summaries need INLA, and spatially varying coefficients also need sn.

Platform support and testing

Every push is tested on GitHub Actions:

Platform R CMD check Model tests with INLA
Linux (Ubuntu) passes (model tests skipped, see below) passes
macOS (Apple silicon) passes (model tests skipped, see below) passes
Windows passes passes

Intel Macs are not tested. Model tests on Linux and macOS run directly with INLA required; on Windows they run inside R CMD check.

Known issue. Inside R CMD check on Linux and macOS, INLA’s own program fails on models with a spatial graph (error: “N simultaneous processes spawned”), while the same models run normally outside R CMD check and on Windows. The package’s checks therefore skip model fitting where INLA cannot fit a small test model, and a separate CI job runs the model tests outside R CMD check. The cause is not yet identified. It has not appeared in any run outside R CMD check.

Workflow

Module Functions What it does
1. Ingest svy_standardize(), svy_from_dhs(), cmc_to_date() Map any survey to a standard schema
2. Boundaries svy_boundaries(), svy_assign_areas() Download GADM, assign clusters to areas
3. Exposure svy_buffers(), svy_extract(), svy_extract_by_year() Displacement-aware buffers, year-matched extraction
4. Structure svy_adjacency() Adjacency graph with island repair
5. Models svy_fit_bym2(), svy_priors() BYM2 + spatially varying coefficients (INLA)
6. Outputs svy_area_effects(), svy_svc_effects(), svy_diagnostics(), svy_map() Posterior summaries, exceedance probabilities, maps 
library(svyexpo)

pts   <- svy_from_dhs(kr, gps, id_vars = c("v001", "v002", "v003", "bidx"))
areas <- svy_boundaries("GHA", level = 2)
pts   <- svy_assign_areas(pts, areas)

expo  <- svy_extract_by_year(svy_buffers(pts), "pm25_2000_2022.tif", name = "pm25")
dat   <- merge(sf::st_drop_geometry(pts), expo, by = "id")

graph <- svy_adjacency(areas)
fit   <- svy_fit_bym2(dat, stunted ~ pm25 + urban, graph, svc = "pm25")
svy_map(svy_svc_effects(fit, "pm25", exponentiate = TRUE), areas)

Run vignette("svyexpo") for a full example on simulated data.

Large rasters

svyexpo never loads a whole raster into memory:

  • terra::rast() opens only the file header.
  • When the area covered by all buffers is small, the raster is cropped to it once. Otherwise exactextractr reads it block by block under each buffer.
  • Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs can be read straight from a URL with "/vsicurl/https://...", downloading only the tiles needed.
  • svy_extract(cache_file = "pm25.parquet") saves the extracted table, so later runs skip the raster entirely.

Data use

DHS data cannot be redistributed. Examples and tests use svy_simulate(); apply for access to real data at https://dhsprogram.com.

Limitations

  • Survey design. INLA fits a model-based analysis and does not use sampling weights. Adjust for the design with stratification variables (for example region and urban/rural) as fixed effects, and consider a cluster-level random effect. For design-based small-area prevalence, use SUMMER or surveyPrev.
  • Location error. Buffers of 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural) account for DHS displacement but do not remove exposure misclassification, and a small share of rural clusters are displaced by up to 10 km.
  • Boundaries. GADM boundaries can differ from the survey’s own administrative boundaries, so some clusters fall in a different area.
  • Calendars. Interview dates from Ethiopia (Ethiopian calendar) and Nepal (Vikram Samvat) are not converted to the Gregorian calendar; a warning is raised.
  • Spatially varying effects. With few clusters per area these estimates are weakly identified and depend on the priors. Report them with exceedance probabilities and check sensitivity to svy_priors().
  • Not yet validated on real survey files. The DHS adapter and the models have been tested on simulated data only. Test on your own data before relying on results. Associations are not necessarily causal.

Status

Experimental. Interfaces may change before version 0.1.0.
